name: Task-justified horizontal overflow
summary: Retain controlled horizontal navigation only for specific content whose use/meaning genuinely requires spatial relationships; reflow ordinary content without loss.
problem: Treating every horizontal scroll as a defect can damage dense tasks, while preserving desktop scroll for ordinary reading can impose unnecessary two-dimensional navigation.
context: Narrow display of data comparison, structured tables or fixed grids contrasted with reading/service content.
observed_solution: Determine whether content has intrinsic two-dimensional requirements; preserve justified spatial arrangement while applying lossless reflow to content that does not require it.
rationale: WCAG SC 1.4.10 explicitly exempts content parts requiring 2D layout for usage/meaning (O05); Carbon documents fixed tiles with optional overflow (O20) and high-density models (O21); GOV.UK offers readable constrained columns and exceptions for wider content (O15).
tradeoffs: Horizontal scrolling may separate labels/context and hinder comparison if poorly structured.
Two-dimensional necessity must be established per task, not inferred from a wide existing design.
applicability: Genuinely 2D comparison or canvas-like regions that cannot be meaningfully reflowed without losing relationships.
non_applicability: Standard explanatory text and single-step forms whose width merely reflects an unchanged desktop container.
accessibility_implications: WCAG 1.4.10 exceptions are specific; keyboard and focus access still require evaluation.
performance_implications: No size/render/scroll performance measurements in this run.
responsive_implications: Select scrolling versus stacking by content/task constraints, not device identity.
implementation_notes: No blanket approval of all overflow-x patterns.
Carbon tile design notes do not themselves prove WCAG exception eligibility.

counterexamples.summary: Ordinary service prose can be shown in a narrow one-column layout without preserving wide desktop scrolling.

version_context: WCAG 2.2 2024, GOV.UK/Carbon/Primer docs unpinned; Carbon excerpts only
